TRACIE CASON.name: Tracie H. Cason
TRACIE CASON.background: Gwinnett Judicial Circuit Superior Court judge since Jan. 1, 2019 (elected 2018 over B.T. Parker and Wesley Person for the seat of retiring Judge Debra Turner; reelected 2022 over Andre Johnson; unopposed 2026). Before the bench, about 21 years as a prosecutor, most recently deputy chief assistant district attorney in Gwinnett, focused on special-victims cases (child molestation, child abuse, sexual assault) as well as murder and drug-trafficking trials. B.A., University of Georgia (1993); J.D., Baylor University School of Law (1997). Lives in Bethlehem; about 22 years in Gwinnett County. Served on advisory board of the CJCC State Expert Committee on Sexual Assault cases, Street Grace and Home of Hope Children's Shelter.
TRACIE CASON.record: Says she cut her civil and domestic caseload in half in her first year and has tried civil and criminal jury trials and presided over hundreds of domestic bench trials and motions.
TRACIE CASON.notes: The 2022 GwinnettForum questionnaire wording is ambiguous about tenure; Patch confirms bench service from Jan. 1, 2019.

positions.stance: Says the court needs "experience, stability, and consistency" after the pandemic backlog; favors proactively scheduling discovery, motions and trial readiness and better managing routine matters so substantive issues get attention.

Names trust in the system as the most pressing issue; says openness about her rulings is "the only way to ensure that our community will trust and respect the judicial process"; "committed to the rule of law and to ensuring that all citizens are protected equally."

statements.text: "My entire career has been centered on protecting our children and this community."
"I have conducted both criminal and civil jury trials as a judge. My opponent has not."
